_comment: Hand-authored. Code that decodes cleanly and fits its neighbours but that nothing in the ROM is known to reach: no operand, no pointer, no target-minus-one pair and no fall-through names it. Each is a LEAD - dead code, or reached some way not yet found.

regions.name: Unreferenced volume-envelope variant
regions.description: Starts LDA $0327,X / BEQ $95F2 and then follows the routine just above it ($95B2-$95F1, which enters the same test after checking $0320 bit 4) step for step: the volume-envelope pointer from $99AB + 2 x index into $1E/$1F, JSR $9627 to fetch the next envelope byte, and the result into $0382,X and $03A5,X. The difference is the arithmetic: this one subtracts $1F and clamps at zero (SBC #$1F / BCS / LDA #$00) where the traced routine ORs in the channel's high nibble. No byte pair $F8 95 or $F9 95 exists in bank 0, no song entry points at $95F8, and no JSR/JMP names it. A LEAD: probably a superseded version left in the ROM. RUN (model, not hardware): with the call at $91F6 patched in memory to JSR $95F9, the 71 songs 1-71 played 1,500 ticks each: 36 of them produce different APU shadow bytes, from the first tick for almost all, and ONLY the four volume registers ($0308, $030C, $0310, $0314) ever differ - song 1: $B8 becomes $A7, $BC becomes $AB (both $11 lower). The variant adds the whole control byte (duty, halt and constant-volume bits included) to the envelope value and subtracts $20 in total, so it clears the constant-volume flag and lowers the volume: audibly different, not a drop-in. Songs 31, 32, 34, 36-48 and others without a volume envelope are unchanged. So it is a discarded alternative volume rule, not a harmless duplicate; nothing reaches it. Still a LEAD for the reason it was dropped.

regions.name: Unreferenced entry: clear nametable rows 0-19 ($C084), then $8B7E
regions.description: LDA #$20 / STA $15 / LDA #$20 / STA $14 / LDA #$00 / STA $17 / LDA #$14 / STA $16 / JSR $C084 ($E453), then falls into $8B7E. $8B7E has callers of its own (JSR at $82EE, $8380 and $87B5, JMP at $82FD); nothing names $8B6B, and the pairs $6B 8B / $6A 8B occur nowhere. It follows an RTS, so it is not a fall-through either. A LEAD. CORRECTION: the name said 'a 32 x 32 area at $1400'. $E453 clears rows `$17` to `$16` - 1 with fill `$14` (page `$15` only gives the first row's address): here rows 0-19 of the nametable at `$2000` with blanks `$20`, which is the area the opening box animation (`$8B7E`) then draws its frame in (the final frame is rows 3-19). The whole ROM was scanned again for `JSR`/`JMP $8B6B` and for the far-call spelling `03 6B 8B`: still nothing, so it stays a lead.

regions.name: Unreferenced tail: store $0560 and $0548
regions.description: STA $0560,X / TYA / STA $0548,X / RTS, right after an RTS. No instruction names $A30F, and the pairs $0F A3 / $0E A3 occur only in bank 5. A LEAD.

regions.name: Unreferenced single-sprite emitter variant
regions.description: CORRECTION: this said it was reached through the fixed-bank entry $C0DC; that slot is `JMP $CF05` (bytes `05 CF`), so $CF2B is not what it reaches. Same shape as $CF05: LDA $83 / AND #$02 / BNE $CF04 (the RTS just before $CF05), save X in $38, then write one hardware sprite at $0200 + $80 from $84 (Y), $87 (tile), $86 (attributes), $85 (X) and JMP $CE5B. $CF05 first parks the sprite off screen (Y = $F8) and writes Y last; this one writes Y first. The byte pairs $2B CF and $2A CF occur nowhere in the ROM and no instruction names $CF2B. A LEAD.

regions.name: Unreferenced memory fill
regions.description: STX $01 / LDX #$00 / STX $00, then STA ($00,X) / INC $00 / BNE back / INC $01 / CPY $01 / BCS back / RTS: fill whole pages with A, from page X through page Y. Sits between traced code and the inline jump table helper at $D6AE. The byte pairs $9B D6 and $9A D6 occur only inside a graphics block, and no instruction names $D69B. A LEAD - the reset path clears RAM by other means.
